Does Quietroom need an electrician?
Absolutely not! We've designed Quietroom with simplicity in mind. Our booth effortlessly plugs into any standard wall socket, powering both the whisper-quiet ventilation fan and the ambient LED lighting with a remarkably efficient 40W. There's no construction, no contractors, and no disruption to your workday — just plug in and enjoy your new oasis of calm. It truly couldn't be easier.
pairs.a:
Does Quietroom need an electrician?
No. Quietroom plugs into any standard wall socket. That one connection runs both the ventilation fan and the LED lighting, and together they draw 40W. You don't need construction or contractors, and setup won't interrupt your workday. Plug it in and the booth is ready to use.
pairs.b: Quietroom doesn't need an electrician. The booth plugs into any standard wall socket, and that one socket powers the ventilation fan and the LED lighting using only 40W. There's no construction and no contractors, so no disruption to your workday. Just plug it in and use it.

💸 Raised our prices by 50% in September. Here's what happened... 👀

Churn? Just 2 out of 140 customers in 2 months. 🤯

(And yes, we grandfathered every existing customer at $8 for 12 months — loyalty matters! 🤝)

Lesson: You're probably undercharging. Seriously. Your customers value what you deliver more than you think. Raise your prices. 🚀

#SaaS #Pricing #BuildInPublic #Startups
pairs.a:
We raised our prices by 50% in September.

In the two months since, 2 of our 140 customers have churned.

Every existing customer was grandfathered at $8 for 12 months, because we wanted to reward the people who stuck with us.

The lesson: you're probably undercharging. Your customers value what you deliver more than you think. Raise your prices.

#SaaS #Pricing #BuildInPublic #Startups
pairs.b: We raised our prices by 50% in September. In the two months since, only 2 of 140 customers have churned. We grandfathered every existing customer at $8 for 12 months. The takeaway from this is that you're probably undercharging, because your customers value what you deliver more than you think, and you should raise your prices.
